reviewedItems.title: Penalty for Arriving Late to the Tee
reviewedItems.question: If you arrive at the tee 3 minutes after your starting time, what is the penalty?

choices.text: You may play but receive a two-stroke penalty
You are disqualified
You can play with no penalty
You receive a warning only

reviewedItems.explanation: If you arrive within five minutes after your starting time, you may play but must add two penalty strokes. Arriving later than five minutes results in disqualification.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl hurries towards the teeing ground where a clock shows she is a few minutes late. Another group of players waits by the tee marker, some looking at their watches.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl arriving late at the tee with a clock visible and other golfers waiting.

reviewedItems.title: Too Many Clubs Discovered After Starting Round
reviewedItems.question: During your round you find that you have more than 14 clubs in your bag. What should you do right away to avoid further penalties?

choices.text: Declare any extra clubs out of play immediately
Keep using all the clubs
Wait until you finish the hole to remove the extras
Give the extra clubs to another player

reviewedItems.explanation: You must instantly declare any clubs over the 14-club limit out of play as soon as you realise it. Leaving them in play will cause additional penalties for each hole you play with too many clubs.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy on the fairway counting his clubs and looking surprised, while another golfer stands nearby.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teen boy counting golf clubs on the fairway, looking surprised, with another player watching.
